selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Swiss Alps, Switzerland

experiences.name: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes
experiences.description: Spend a full day skiing across the world-famous Jungfrau ski region, which connects Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren with over 200km of groomed pistes. Ideal for all skill levels, families can enjoy gentle beginner runs while more experienced skiers tackle challenging black runs with breathtaking Alpine panoramas.

experiences.name: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride
experiences.description: Board the legendary Glacier Express panoramic train for a family-friendly journey through dramatic Alpine landscapes, crossing 291 bridges and passing through 91 tunnels. The 8-hour scenic route connects Zermatt to St. Moritz and offers stunning views of snow-capped peaks, frozen rivers, and charming Swiss villages.
experiences.location: Zermatt to St. Moritz, Valais & Graubünden

experiences.name: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Making Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on culinary workshop in a traditional Alpine chalet where a local chef teaches your family how to prepare authentic Swiss cheese fondue and raclette. Learn about the centuries-old cheesemaking traditions of the region, taste local Gruyère and Emmental varieties, and enjoy your creations with Swiss bread and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Snow Tubing and Sledging at Fiesch
experiences.description: A thrilling family-friendly winter activity where everyone from toddlers to grandparents can enjoy high-speed snow tubing runs and traditional wooden sledge tracks. The Fiesch resort offers dedicated family snow parks with safe, supervised runs, hot chocolate stations, and equipment rental included in the ticket price.

experiences.name: Matterhorn Glacier Paradise Cable Car Experience
experiences.description: Take the highest cable car in the Alps up to 3,883 meters to the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise observation deck for jaw-dropping 360-degree views of 14 countries and 38 Alpine peaks. Explore the glacier palace ice caves, walk across the glacier on a guided family tour, and enjoy year-round skiing on pristine glacier snow.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Swiss Alps, Switzerland

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Geneva Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage, clear customs, and arrange pre-booked budget transfer or take the cost-effective Swiss train/bus connection toward the Swiss Alps region. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your accommodation. Review the resort amenities and plan the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at departure airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at departure airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the airport (Migros or Coop grocery stores inside the terminal offer sandwiches and snacks for CHF 5-10) before or after landing

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport-to-resort transfer in advance to save money. Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) night connections are economical. Keep snacks handy as late-night dining options near resort may be limited. Exchange some currency or withdraw CHF at the airport ATM for small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery after late arrival. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort or a nearby bakery. Take a gentle orientation walk around the resort and the nearest village to get familiar with the surroundings, locate ski rental shops, and scout out budget-friendly dining options for the week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the local ski rental shop and rent ski equipment for the family at budget rates (look for multi-day rental packages which offer better value). Purchase a beginner or half-day ski lift pass and head to the nearest beginner ski slopes. Take a short introductory ski lesson if family members are new to skiing — group lessons are far more affordable than private ones.
day_by_day.evening: Return ski equipment to the locker at the resort. Warm up with hot chocolate at the resort lounge or a local mountain café. Explore the village on foot, browse local shops, and enjoy the Alpine evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Coop or Migros supermarket near the resort for bread, cheese, cold cuts, and yogurt — self-catered breakfast keeps costs very low (CHF 5-8 per person)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from the supermarket to eat on the slopes — slope-side restaurants are expensive in Switzerland
meals.dinner: Find a local Stübli (traditional Swiss pub-restaurant) in the village offering fondue or rösti dishes for CHF 18-25 per person — look for daily specials (Tagesmenü)

day_by_day.notes: Multi-day ski passes and equipment rental packages offer significant savings over single-day rates. Group ski lessons for children and adults are available at most Swiss ski schools at a fraction of private lesson costs. Always check resort notice boards for discount vouchers.

day_by_day.morning: Full day of skiing! Start early to maximize your lift pass value. Head to the intermediate slopes if the family is gaining confidence, or continue on beginner runs. Ski schools often offer structured morning group lessons — enroll children in ski school for a fun and educational morning on the snow.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a packed lunch on the mountain, explore different ski runs and lifts. Try a scenic gondola or chairlift ride to higher elevation for panoramic Alpine views even if you ski back down on easier routes. Older children and adults can attempt a blue-rated run with supervision.
day_by_day.evening: After skiing, enjoy a family-friendly snowshoeing walk or a gentle evening stroll through the illuminated village. Many Swiss Alpine villages have free ice skating rinks or toboggan runs that are affordable and great family fun.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort room using supermarket supplies — oatmeal, fruit, bread, and cheese (CHF 3-6 per person)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket eaten at a mountain rest area or picnic bench — thermos of hot soup or hot chocolate saves money and keeps you warm
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal in the resort room if kitchen facilities are available, or visit a local pizzeria or kebab/döner shop in the village for budget-friendly options (CHF 12-18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Swiss ski schools (Schweizer Skischule) are reputable and offer structured group lessons for all ages. Toboggan runs (Schlittelbahn) are often free or very low cost and are a huge hit with families. Check if the resort has a family ski pass deal.

day_by_day.morning: Take a well-deserved rest from skiing. Enjoy a slow morning and then take a scenic winter hike on a designated winter walking trail near the resort. Most Alpine resorts maintain groomed winter walking paths that are free to use and offer stunning mountain scenery without the cost of lift passes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Swiss Alpine museum or visitor center to learn about the region's history, culture, and mountain traditions — many are free or have minimal entry fees. Alternatively, visit a nearby traditional Swiss village by local bus (PostBus Switzerland is affordable and scenic) to explore local architecture and craft shops.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a classic Swiss fondue or raclette dinner experience — this is a must-do cultural experience. Look for a mid-range local restaurant offering a fondue set menu for families, which is more economical than à la carte.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery (Bäckerei) for fresh croissants, Gipfeli (Swiss croissants), and coffee — a treat that is still budget-friendly at CHF 6-10 per person
meals.lunch: Migros or Coop restaurant inside a supermarket — these offer hot daily meals at very reasonable Swiss prices (CHF 10-14 per person) and are popular with locals
meals.dinner: Traditional Swiss restaurant for cheese fondue — budget CHF 22-28 per person for a fondue set; children's portions are usually available at reduced prices

day_by_day.notes: Rest days are important for muscle recovery, especially for beginners. Winter walking trails are clearly marked and safe for families. PostBus Switzerland passes can be purchased for regional travel at discounted rates — check the SBB app for current fares.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the ski slopes refreshed! Today focus on trying a new ski area or sector of the mountain. Many Swiss resorts offer interconnected ski areas accessible on the same lift pass. Challenge yourselves with slightly more advanced runs while staying within your comfort zone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try an exciting family winter activity: tobogganing on a designated toboggan run (Schlittelbahn). Many resorts have dedicated toboggan tracks ranging from gentle family runs to more thrilling options. Sled rentals are inexpensive and the activity is one of the most fun and affordable in the Alps.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost après-ski cultural event in the village — many resorts host free outdoor concerts, fire shows, or folk music evenings during the ski season. Enjoy a warm Glühwein (mulled wine) for adults or Kinderpunsch (non-alcoholic mulled fruit punch) for children at an outdoor stall.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort — scrambled eggs, bread, fruit, and hot drinks prepared in room
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of hot soup and sandwiches for the slopes — save money and stay energized
meals.dinner: Visit a local Bergrestaurant (mountain restaurant) for an early dinner before heading back down — look for a Tagesmenü (daily set menu) which offers soup, main course, and sometimes dessert for CHF 18-22

day_by_day.notes: Toboggan runs are one of Switzerland's best-kept budget secrets for families — check resort maps for locations. Glühwein stalls are a quintessential Alpine evening experience. Keep an eye on the resort's event calendar posted at the tourist information office.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a different winter sport: try cross-country skiing (Langlauf) on groomed Nordic trails, which are typically much cheaper than downhill skiing as no lift pass is required. Equipment rental for cross-country skiing is also significantly less expensive. This is a great low-impact activity for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local indoor swimming pool or thermal spa if available near the resort — many Swiss Alpine towns have affordable public pools and wellness facilities that are perfect for warming up tired muscles. Alternatively, build a snowman or have a family snowball fight in a safe open area near the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Prepare a budget-friendly family dinner together using ingredients from the local supermarket — Swiss supermarkets stock excellent quality cheese, bread, cured meats, and vegetables for a hearty self-catered meal. This is the most economical dinner option and can be a fun family activity.

meals.breakfast: Supermarket supplies — yogurt, muesli, fruit, and juice (CHF 3-5 per person)
meals.lunch: Village café or bakery for a warm soup and bread roll — many offer a simple lunch special for CHF 8-12
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner in resort room — Swiss cheese platter, charcuterie, fresh bread, and a simple pasta dish purchased from Migros or Coop (CHF 8-12 per person total)

day_by_day.notes: Cross-country skiing trails (Loipen) are marked on resort maps and are often free or require only a small trail fee. Public swimming pools in Switzerland are very clean and well-maintained. Self-catering for at least 2-3 dinners during the trip is the single biggest way to reduce costs in Switzerland.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning ski session or a last winter walk to soak in the Alpine scenery. Take photos of the mountain landscape and village. Purchase any Swiss souvenirs within budget — Migros and Coop sell affordable Swiss chocolate, which makes excellent gifts (Lindt, Frey, or Cailler brands at supermarket prices are far cheaper than souvenir shops).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage with the hotel concierge if checkout is before departure. Take a final stroll through the village, visit the local tourist office to collect any free maps or brochures as mementos, and make your way to the train or bus station for the journey back to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to Zurich or Geneva Airport via Swiss Federal Railways or PostBus. Allow ample travel time — Swiss trains are punctual but Alpine routes can take 2-4 hours depending on your resort location. Enjoy a final Swiss meal at the airport Coop or Migros before your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast using remaining supermarket supplies or a quick stop at the resort café
meals.lunch: Pack remaining food for the journey or grab a Coop/Migros sandwich at the train station (CHF 5-8)
meals.dinner: Airport Coop or Migros restaurant for an affordable final Swiss meal before the flight home (CHF 10-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the resort. Book your return train tickets in advance via the SBB app for the best prices. Swiss trains to airports run frequently and are very reliable. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before international departure. Carry any purchased Swiss cheese in checked luggage to avoid issues at security.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Collect luggage and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Swiss Alps (approximately 2-3 hour scenic drive or train connection depending on exact resort location). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront-style Alpine suite. Familiarize yourself with the resort amenities and grab a light welcome snack at the hotel bar.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack or light bite at the Aegean Bliss Resort hotel bar/lounge upon arrival — expect CHF 15–25 per person for cold cuts, cheese board, and warm drinks

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 completely relaxed. Pre-arrange an airport transfer or private shuttle through the resort to avoid stress after a long flight. Pack layers in your carry-on as Alpine temperatures in February can drop to -10°C or below. Confirm resort check-in accepts late arrivals — most Alpine resorts do but it is worth verifying in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast. After breakfast, take a relaxed walk around the resort and nearby village to get your bearings. Visit the local ski rental shop to rent equipment for the family — skis, boots, poles, and helmets. If any family members are beginners, book ski school lessons starting tomorrow morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest beginner-friendly slopes adjacent to the resort for a gentle warm-up ski session. Spend 2–3 hours on easy green and blue runs to shake off jet lag and get the family's ski legs going. More experienced skiers can explore a few intermediate blue runs nearby. Return to the resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort's wellness facilities — sauna, hot tub, or indoor pool — to soothe muscles after the first ski session. Enjoy a family dinner at a mid-range Alpine restaurant in the village.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — included or CHF 20–30 per person if not included
meals.lunch: Mountain hut lunch on the slopes — try a traditional Rösti (Swiss potato cake) with a hot chocolate or soup, budget CHF 20–30 per person
meals.dinner: Village restaurant dinner — try Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (sliced veal in cream sauce) or Alpine pasta dishes, budget CHF 35–50 per person

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag may still be a factor today, so avoid over-scheduling. Hydrate well as Alpine altitude can cause mild dehydration. Apply high-SPF sunscreen even on cloudy days — UV rays are significantly stronger at altitude. Ski rental shops often offer multi-day packages that are more economical than day-by-day rentals.

day_by_day.morning: Early start with a hearty breakfast. Travel to the Jungfrau ski region connecting Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren — one of the most iconic ski areas in the world. Purchase Jungfrau Top Ski Region passes (approximately CHF 75–90 per adult per day, CHF 40–50 for children). Beginners can join ski school while experienced family members hit the wide, well-groomed blue and red runs of Grindelwald First or Kleine Scheidegg.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing across the interconnected Jungfrau slopes. Take the Eiger Express gondola for breathtaking views of the Eiger North Face. Intermediate skiers should try the classic run from Kleine Scheidegg down to Grindelwald Grund. Enjoy a mid-slope lunch at one of the mountain restaurants with panoramic Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort, shower and rest. Head out for a cozy fondue dinner in the village to celebrate a great first full ski day.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fuel up with eggs, bread, cold cuts, and coffee before a big ski day
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant on Jungfrau slopes — try Berner Platte (assorted meats and sauerkraut) or a hearty Alpine soup with bread, CHF 25–35 per person
meals.dinner: Traditional Swiss fondue restaurant in the village — cheese fondue for the table with bread, pickles, and pearl onions, CHF 35–55 per person

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Jungfrau ski passes online in advance for a 10–15% discount. The Jungfrau region is best accessed from Grindelwald or Interlaken by train — check the Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) schedule the evening before. Wear moisture-wicking base layers under ski gear. Children under 9 often ski free with a paying adult on Jungfrau passes.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head to the train station to board the legendary Glacier Express panoramic train — one of the most scenic rail journeys in the world. The classic route runs from Zermatt to St. Moritz (or vice versa) passing through dramatic Alpine valleys, viaducts, and snow-covered mountain passes. Book seats in the panoramic dining car for the full experience. Adult tickets approximately CHF 130–160 (reservation fee CHF 13–20 extra); children receive discounts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Glacier Express journey through the Oberalp Pass and Rhine Gorge — often called the 'Swiss Grand Canyon.' Enjoy the ever-changing Alpine scenery from the comfort of the heated panoramic carriages. Arrive at the destination station and spend an hour or two exploring the charming mountain village before returning by train.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort's own restaurant or a nearby mid-range eatery, keeping the evening light as tomorrow is another active day.

meals.breakfast: Quick resort breakfast or grab fresh pastries and coffee from a local bakery near the train station — CHF 8–15 per person
meals.lunch: Lunch served onboard the Glacier Express dining car — a set three-course Alpine meal included with some ticket classes or available for CHF 35–50 per person; reservation recommended
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or nearby village bistro — try Älplermagronen (Alpine mac and cheese with applesauce) or a simple Raclette, CHF 30–45 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Glacier Express is a full-day commitment — the complete journey takes approximately 8 hours. If traveling with younger children, consider doing just a scenic segment (e.g., Andermatt to Zermatt, about 3 hours) rather than the full route. Book Glacier Express seats well in advance as they sell out quickly in ski season. The Swiss Travel Pass offers significant discounts if you plan multiple train journeys.

day_by_day.date: 2027-02-19 (Friday) - Snow Tubing, Sledging & Fondue Making Class
day_by_day.morning: Head to Fiesch for a thrilling snow tubing and sledging session — a perfect family-friendly activity suitable for all ages from toddlers to grandparents. The Fiesch snow park offers dedicated tubing lanes, natural sledge runs, and a fun snow play area. Equipment is available to rent on-site. Spend 2–3 hours enjoying the snowy slopes without the pressure of skiing technique.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to a traditional Alpine chalet for the Swiss Cheese and Fondue Making Class. A local chef guides the family through the art of making authentic Swiss cheese fondue, raclette, and possibly homemade bread. Learn about the history of Swiss cheese culture, try different regional varieties, and of course eat everything you make. The class typically lasts 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort with full stomachs and happy memories. Enjoy a light evening at the resort — hot chocolate by the fireplace, board games, or a gentle swim in the indoor pool. Keep dinner light given the afternoon's indulgent fondue feast.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — stock up before a full activity day
meals.lunch: Light snack at the Fiesch snow park café — hot dogs, warm drinks, and pastries, CHF 10–18 per person
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the resort bar or a nearby café — soup, salad, and sandwiches, CHF 20–30 per person (you will likely still be full from the fondue class!)

day_by_day.notes: Snow tubing at Fiesch is weather-dependent — check conditions the evening before. The fondue making class should be booked in advance as group sessions fill up quickly in peak ski season. Wear warm, waterproof clothing for the snow tubing session as it involves more sitting and sliding than skiing. The cooking class is a wonderful cultural experience and a great souvenir skill to bring home.

day_by_day.date: 2027-02-20 (Saturday) - Matterhorn Glacier Paradise Cable Car Experience
day_by_day.morning: Early departure to Zermatt — the car-free Alpine village at the foot of the iconic Matterhorn. Take the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise cable car, the highest cable car in the Alps, ascending to 3,883 meters above sea level. At the summit, visit the Glacier Palace ice cave, step onto the viewing platform for 360-degree views of 38 Alpine peaks, and cross into Italy on the glacier. Adults approximately CHF 95–110; children CHF 55–65. Dress in your warmest layers — temperatures at the summit can reach -20°C with wind chill.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Zermatt and spend the afternoon exploring this charming car-free village. Browse the main Bahnhofstrasse for Swiss souvenirs, chocolate, and watches. Visit the Matterhorn Museum (Zermatlantis) for a fascinating look at early Alpine mountaineering history. If energy permits, enjoy a few runs on the Zermatt ski area — one of the finest in the world with guaranteed snow at high altitude.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a special dinner in Zermatt before returning to the resort — treat the family to a slightly elevated dining experience to celebrate an unforgettable day beneath the Matterhorn.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — pack snacks for the cable car journey
meals.lunch: Summit restaurant at Matterhorn Glacier Paradise (3,883m) — a truly unique dining experience; expect CHF 30–45 per person for a hot meal with the world's best views
meals.dinner: Zermatt restaurant dinner — try Valais-style lamb or beef Fondue Bourguignonne (meat fondue), CHF 45–65 per person; Brown Cow Pub or Walliserkanne are popular mid-range options

day_by_day.notes: Altitude sickness is a real concern at 3,883m — ascend slowly and avoid overexertion at the summit. Children and elderly family members should spend no more than 30–45 minutes at the very top. Zermatt is car-free so you must park in Täsch and take the shuttle train (CHF 8–10 return per person). Book the cable car tickets online in advance to avoid long queues on weekends. The Matterhorn is most photogenic in the morning light.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy one final morning on the slopes near the resort — a bittersweet but satisfying last ski session. Return any rented equipment by the designated time (usually 11:00–12:00). Take a final gondola or chairlift ride to soak in the Alpine panorama one last time. Snap family photos on the mountain before heading back down.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for checkout. Pack bags and enjoy a leisurely lunch in the village. If time allows before departure transfers, visit a local Alpine shop to pick up final souvenirs — Swiss chocolate, cheese, cuckoo clocks, or a bottle of Swiss Kirsch. Begin the transfer back toward the airport or onward destination.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from the Swiss Alps with incredible memories. If your flight is the following day, consider an overnight stay near Zurich Airport to avoid an exhausting same-day rush. Enjoy a final Swiss dinner near the airport or in Zurich city center.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — enjoy it fully before checkout
meals.lunch: Village farewell lunch — try a Bratwurst with Rösti at a local mountain restaurant or a simple café, CHF 20–30 per person
meals.dinner: Airport area or Zurich city dinner — try Zeughauskeller in Zurich for classic Swiss cuisine in a historic setting, CHF 35–50 per person

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the resort and arrange luggage storage if you want to ski in the morning before leaving. Swiss chocolate and cheese make excellent gifts — purchase vacuum-packed cheese for international travel. Keep receipts for VAT refund claims (non-EU travelers can reclaim Swiss VAT of 7.7% on purchases over CHF 300 at the airport). Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Zurich Airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (travel day)

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely gourmet breakfast at the resort's alpine restaurant to recover from travel. Afterward, visit the resort's ski concierge to collect pre-fitted rental equipment, premium ski boots, and Jungfrau region lift passes. Orientation session with a private ski instructor for the family — warm-up runs on beginner and intermediate slopes near the resort base.
day_by_day.afternoon: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes: Spend the afternoon skiing across the world-famous Jungfrau ski region, which connects Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. With a private certified ski guide, explore groomed blue and red runs suited to all family skill levels. Take the iconic Männlichen gondola for sweeping Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau panoramas between runs. Hot chocolate break at a mountain-top sun terrace restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a private spa session — alpine herb sauna, heated indoor pool, and family relaxation suite. Dress for a fine-dining dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet alpine breakfast buffet at the resort — freshly baked pastries, Swiss Bircher muesli, smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, artisan cheeses, and fresh-pressed juices.
meals.lunch: Mountain-top lunch at Restaurant Grindelwald First or Berghaus Männlichen — raclette, alpine soup, and Wiener Schnitzel with a panoramic terrace view.
meals.dinner: Signature fine-dining dinner at the resort's premium restaurant — four-course menu featuring pan-seared lake trout, truffle risotto, Swiss beef tenderloin, and a decadent chocolate fondant with Gruyère ice cream. Paired with a curated Swiss wine flight.

day_by_day.notes: Book private ski instructor at least 48 hours in advance through the resort. Ensure children have properly fitted helmets and ski gear. Jungfrau lift passes can be loaded onto a single family card for convenience. Weather permitting — check daily snow and visibility reports each morning.

day_by_day.morning: Snow Tubing and Sledging at Fiesch: Depart after breakfast via private resort transfer to Fiesch for a thrilling family-friendly winter morning. Enjoy high-speed snow tubing runs, traditional Swiss wooden sledges on dedicated family runs, and snowplay areas suitable for all ages — from toddlers to grandparents. Professional activity guides ensure safety and maximum fun. Warm up with hot chocolate and pretzels at the Fiesch activity lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Jungfrau region for a second afternoon of Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes. Focus on more adventurous red and black runs for confident skiers while younger family members continue with their private ski instructor on groomed blue runs. Optional: Snowboard lesson for teens with a certified instructor.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski experience: Visit a traditional alpine wine and cheese bar in Grindelwald village. Enjoy a curated raclette and fondue tasting paired with Chasselas and Pinot Gris wines. Private horse-drawn sleigh ride back to the resort through snow-lit alpine meadows.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort — Swiss rösti with poached eggs, smoked alpine ham, freshly baked croissants, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Casual mountain lodge lunch at Fiesch activity center — hearty alpine lentil soup, grilled bratwurst with sauerkraut, and warm apple strudel.
meals.dinner: Traditional Swiss fondue and raclette dinner at Chalet Restaurant Grindelwald — premium Gruyère and Vacherin fondue, charcuterie platters, roasted potatoes, and cornichons. Paired with Swiss dry white wine.

day_by_day.notes: Private resort transfer to Fiesch is approximately 45–60 minutes — arrange the night before. Snow tubing at Fiesch is suitable for children aged 3 and above. Sleigh ride should be booked through the concierge in advance. Dress in waterproof layers for outdoor activities.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride: Board the legendary Glacier Express panoramic train for a family-friendly journey through dramatic Alpine scenery. Depart from Zermatt or St. Moritz (private transfer arranged by resort) and travel through 91 tunnels and over 291 bridges, passing glaciers, gorges, and snow-covered valleys. Reserve premium first-class seats with panoramic windows and optional Excellence Class dining for an elevated on-board experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Matterhorn Glacier Paradise Cable Car Experience: Upon arriving near Zermatt, take the highest cable car in the Alps up to 3,883 meters to the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise observation deck. Experience breathtaking 360-degree views of 38 Alpine peaks across four countries. Visit the Glacier Palace ice cave, walk on the glacier, and enjoy the Snow Fun Park. Private guide provides geological and cultural context throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Gourmet dinner in Zermatt village — one of Switzerland's most exclusive car-free alpine towns. Stroll the charming pedestrian streets lit by lanterns before dinner at a Michelin-recognized alpine restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — continental spread with Swiss yogurt, seasonal berries, freshly squeezed orange juice, and espresso.
meals.lunch: Excellence Class on-board dining on the Glacier Express — three-course curated menu with regional specialties, Swiss wines, and panoramic views rolling past.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Restaurant Après Post Hotel or Chez Vrony in Zermatt — seasonal alpine tasting menu featuring venison carpaccio, truffle pasta, roasted lamb rack, and a selection of Swiss artisan cheeses. Paired with Valais Grand Cru wines.

day_by_day.notes: Glacier Express seats must be reserved well in advance — Excellence Class is highly recommended for the premium experience. The cable car to Matterhorn Glacier Paradise may be subject to weather and wind closures; have a backup indoor activity planned. Altitude at 3,883m can cause mild altitude sickness — stay hydrated and ascend slowly. Private transfer back to the resort from Zermatt in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Making Class: Join a hands-on culinary workshop in a traditional Alpine chalet where a local chef teaches the family the authentic art of Swiss cheese-making and fondue preparation. Learn the history of Gruyère and Emmental, stir the copper vat, and create your own fondue blend using regional cheeses, white wine, and kirsch. Perfect for all ages — children will love the interactive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes: Return to the slopes for a final premium ski afternoon. With two days of practice behind you, explore the more scenic and challenging runs of the Jungfrau region. Private guide leads the family on a curated 'best of Jungfrau' ski tour — stopping at iconic viewpoints and hidden mountain restaurants. Optional: Heli-skiing experience for adventurous adults (subject to availability and weather).
day_by_day.evening: Luxury spa and wellness evening at the resort. Private family spa suite booking — including heated pool, steam room, alpine hay bath, and a couples' or family massage treatment. End the evening with a private fondue dinner in your suite using the cheese you made this morning.

meals.breakfast: Resort gourmet breakfast — eggs your way, Swiss muesli, smoked mountain trout, artisan pastries, and premium coffee selection.
meals.lunch: Post-class tasting lunch at the chalet — enjoy the fondue and cheeses you created in the workshop, accompanied by crusty bread, charcuterie, and local white wine or sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Private in-suite fondue and raclette dinner — curated by the resort chef using your handcrafted cheese from the morning class. Accompanied by a bottle of Fendant white wine and a decadent Swiss chocolate dessert platter.

day_by_day.notes: The cheese-making class typically runs 2–3 hours and should be booked through the resort concierge or directly with the local chalet operator. Minimum age for participation is usually 5 years. Heli-skiing must be arranged 48 hours in advance and is weather-dependent. The private spa suite requires advance booking — reserve as early as possible.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning for leisure and family relaxation. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and explore the resort's facilities — indoor heated pool, kids' snow play area, or a guided snowshoe walk around the resort grounds with a naturalist guide. Optional: Visit the resort boutique for Swiss watches, chocolates, and alpine souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise area or Jungfrau region for a final afternoon of skiing and winter sports. Alternatively, opt for a private ice skating session at a nearby alpine rink, followed by a guided cross-country skiing trail through a pristine snow-covered forest — a serene and scenic experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the resort's most prestigious dining venue. Multi-course chef's tasting menu celebrating Swiss alpine cuisine at its finest. Live ambient Swiss folk music performance. Toast to the journey with a bottle of vintage Swiss champagne or Dom Pérignon.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely à la carte brunch at the resort — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, truffle scrambled eggs, Swiss waffles with berry compote, fresh juice, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Slope-side lunch at a premium mountain restaurant — Caesar salad, pan-seared perch fillet from Lake Thun, and warm apple tart with vanilla cream.
meals.dinner: Seven-course farewell chef's tasting menu at the resort's gala restaurant — featuring foie gras terrine, lobster bisque, Wagyu beef with black truffle, and a Grand Marnier soufflé. Paired with a premium Swiss and French wine pairing curated by the head sommelier.

day_by_day.notes: Reserve the farewell gala dinner table at least 3 days in advance — request a window table with alpine views and inform staff of any dietary restrictions or special celebrations. Consider arranging a professional family photo session on the slopes or at a scenic alpine viewpoint in the afternoon as a lasting memory.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps. Wake up early for a last sunrise walk or snowshoe stroll around the resort grounds to soak in the alpine scenery. Pack and prepare for checkout. Visit the resort spa for a final express treatment — revitalizing facial or hot stone massage to prepare for travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Checkout from Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury chauffeur transfer to Zurich Airport or relevant departure hub. En route, stop at a local artisan chocolate shop or delicatessen in a nearby village to pick up premium Swiss chocolates, cheeses, and gifts — Läderach, Sprüngli, or a local alpine producer.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Arrive at the airport with ample time. Enjoy the premium lounge facilities before boarding. Reflect on an extraordinary week of skiing, alpine adventures, culinary experiences, and family memories in the heart of the Swiss Alps.

meals.breakfast: Final resort gourmet breakfast — a generous spread of Swiss pastries, smoked meats, artisan cheeses, poached eggs, fresh fruit, and a farewell hot chocolate for the family.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort or a charming alpine café en route to the airport — croque monsieur, alpine vegetable soup, and a slice of Swiss carrot cake (Rüeblitorte).
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or on-board premium cabin meal — request special dietary preferences through your airline in advance for a comfortable return journey.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–3.5 hours for transfer from the Swiss Alps to Zurich Airport depending on exact resort location and road conditions. Confirm private transfer booking the night before. Arrange luggage shipping for ski equipment if not checking it through. Request a late checkout from the resort (subject to availability) to maximize your final morning. Keep Swiss francs on hand for last-minute tips and small purchases.

query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February 2026
